title: Psychology Paper 6: Development, Learning and Study Methods
source: Adapted from user-provided Psychology development and study methods set

objective.question: The process of toilet training to children occurs during the stage:
objective.explanation: Toilet training occurs during the anal stage.

objective.question: Death instinct is:
objective.explanation: Death instinct (Thanatos) is the destructive drive; aggression may express it.

objective.question: According to Erik Erikson, when do humans develop a sense of trust or mistrust:
objective.explanation: Trust vs mistrust is the first year stage.

objective.question: A person who eats and smokes a great deal is most likely to have been fixated during the:
objective.explanation: Oral fixation links with oral behaviours.

objective.question: During cognitive development, an egocentric child:
options: Can evaluate events only in terms of their personal consequences
Can imagine how another person feels
objective.explanation: Egocentrism means viewing events from one's own perspective.

objective.question: Kohlberg's level of moral development which includes understanding that social system has an interest in people's behavior is called:
objective.explanation: Conventional level upholds social order.

objective.question: Developmental psychologists study children in order to understand how they develop:
objective.explanation: Development covers emotional, cognitive and social domains.

objective.question: Psychosexual stage of development that directs a child's activity to the genital parts of the body:
objective.explanation: The phallic stage focuses on genital interest.

objective.question: The SQ3R study method stands for:
objective.explanation: SQ3R is Survey, Question, Read, Recite, Review.

objective.question: Which personality type is characterized by being competitive, time-conscious and hostile?
objective.explanation: Type A is competitive and time-conscious.

objective.question: Learning that involves an association of stimulus and response is seen in the theory of:
objective.explanation: Classical conditioning links stimulus and response.

objective.question: The part of personality that operates on the reality principle is:
objective.explanation: The ego follows the reality principle.

objective.question: A negative feeling towards individuals based on their belonging in a given group is called:
objective.explanation: Prejudice is negative evaluation by group.

objective.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a good communication channel?
objective.explanation: Ambiguity is a poor channel quality.

objective.question: Accommodation and Assimilation are concepts explained by:
objective.explanation: Piaget described assimilation and accommodation.

objective.question: Defense mechanism where one transfers emotion from one situation to another is:
objective.explanation: Displacement redirects emotion to a substitute.

objective.question: Social psychology is the systematic study of:
objective.explanation: Social psychology studies behaviour in social life.

objective.question: The stage of psychosexual development where sexual feelings are repressed is:
objective.explanation: Latency is the quiet phase.

objective.question: Effective reading that involves quickly looking through a book to get general ideas is called:
objective.explanation: Skimming gives general ideas; scanning finds specifics.

objective.question: A status people acquire by virtue of their occupation, income or education is called:
objective.explanation: Achieved status is earned.

structured.question: Name four factors which can influence the learning process positively or negatively. (2 marks)
markingGuide: Four factors such as motivation, environment, health, methods: 2 marks.
structured.modelAnswer: Motivation, prior knowledge, environment and study methods influence learning.

structured.question: List two teaching methods and state two advantages for each. (5 marks)
markingGuide: Two advantages of first method: 2 marks.
Two advantages of second method: 2 marks.
structured.modelAnswer: Lecture and discussion are examples; lecture covers much content efficiently while discussion promotes participation.

structured.question: State five ways a student can use the five senses when studying. (3 marks)
structured.modelAnswer: Reading, listening, viewing diagrams, hands-on practice and verbal rehearsal.

structured.question: List five types of examinations and give three reasons why it is important to assess performance. (5 marks)
structured.modelAnswer: Written, oral, practical, continuous and objective exams; assessment measures learning and guides teaching.

structured.question: Outline how to improve skills in writing an assignment or essay. Show how a student can use 24 hours effectively. (8 marks)
markingGuide: Writing skills such as planning and referencing: 4 marks.
Time use across study, rest and duties: 4 marks.
structured.modelAnswer: Plan, research, draft, revise and reference; balance study, classes, rest, meals and revision in 24 hours.
